newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine predicts better grain crop, higher exports.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine predicts better grain crop, higher exports.

text.p: Ukraine's winter wheat crop will be 36 percent above 1996's net 13.1 million tonnes, and officials are sticking to predictions that 1997 net grain output will be 35 million tonnes, the agriculture minister said on Thursday.

Mykhailo Zubets, who also holds the post of deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, also told a news conference that Ukraine's grain exports would double this year from 1996's official three million tonnes.

"We will have 36 percent more winter wheat that last year," Zubets said. He also predicted this year's maize crop would be "significantly better" than the 1.8 million tonnes harvested last year. The maize crop in 1995 stood at 2.2 million tonnes.
Agricultural experts have said previously that the 1997 grain crop was progressing well. A drought last year was blamed for a paltry 25.4 million tonne grain harvest.

Ukraine has completed sowing of 13.51 million hectares to grain, up from last year's 13.12 million hectares. Private farmers have planted 4.647 million hectares with early spring grain, practically unchanged from last year.

"Grain is a top priority for us to improve the situation in the agricultural sector," Zubets said. He said the sector was riddled with problems of fuel and money shortages and a lack of spare parts for machinery.
